title: Chilla and i'tikaf
summary: What a chilla is, how Hazrat links it to i'tikaf, and why the thought on one point is 'the soul of worship'.

blocks.q: A chilla means sitting for forty days, so that the worship done in them becomes a routine. In those forty days a special blessing descends, and for us it brings benefit both inwardly and outwardly.

blocks.p: Hazrat reads that at the beginning of the wahi, the Prophet ﷺ would go to the cave of Hira and take with him provisions that would not spoil for eight days. Such food, the book says, cannot be meat or ghee, and from this comes tark-e-haiwanat, giving up animal foods.

'What is a chilla? It is i'tikaf,' Hazrat says. The Prophet ﷺ sat in i'tikaf in Ramadan, and some of his blessed wives did too. Some elders sit in i'tikaf for a week, two weeks or three days; it can be for even one day. Hazrat mentions that the Hanafi and Shafi'i madhabs differ on its conditions, and then encourages everyone:

blocks.q: Everyone goes to the masjid. Make the intention of i'tikaf for an hour or two: what harm is there? We should do it.
In i'tikaf a person is turned wholly toward worship. His thought becomes fixed on one point. Complete attention is the soul of worship.

blocks.p: Hazrat gives the opposite as a lesson: a man who prayed regularly, but with a scattered mind, went over the accounts of his four shops, one in each rakat. When the imam finished, he complained that only three rakats had been prayed, because he had not yet reached his fourth shop. 'He had been reading the book of accounts, not the book of the heart.' There is no benefit, Hazrat says, in namaz without a gathered heart.

Some elders keep Saum-e-Maryam along with i'tikaf: fasting all day and speaking to no one, as Bibi Maryam, in obedience to Allah's command, spoke to no one. 'That is why, in chillas, Saum-e-Maryam has its importance: silence.' Hazrat reads that in our time too, special servants of Allah spend two or three months in i'tikaf and keep Saum-e-Maryam.
He also describes Hizbul Bahr, read in the way of the elders with fasting and silence, and speaks of giving permission for it.

blocks.note: Ask your teacher before taking up a chilla, Saum-e-Maryam or Hizbul Bahr. Parts 6 to 9 are not yet public on YouTube, so these passages have no video link yet. Parts of the part 8 recording were not transcribed (0:56-1:44, 12:07-12:33, 15:16-17:17, 27:11-27:41, 30:23-30:55).
